_what: DEFECT — a COMPOSITE's PIPEREV is not the code that built it. It is inherited from whichever member was the registration reference.

measured.reading: both composites carry their reference member's stamp exactly; neither carries the building code's

mechanism: siril `stack` propagates the reference image's header into the output. stamp_headers.sh's header_composite_provenance_lines exists precisely to REPLACE inherited keys, and its KEYS tuple (DISTMODL DISTA DISTB DISTC DISTNORM DISTRHO ...) does NOT include PIPEREV. So the inherited value survives unchallenged.
why_it_matters: CLAUDE.md states 'PIPEREV is git rev-parse --short HEAD (stamp_headers.sh), so a commit stamps every artifact built after it'. That is TRUE for members and FALSE for composites. Any reasoning that dates a composite from its PIPEREV — including a scope decision about whether a rebuild is needed — is reading the wrong commit. This is the same failure class the stamper's own docstring describes for CALSET: 'worse than an absent stamp: a gate reading it is told a confident falsehood.'
how_it_was_found: the REGREF stamp added in this unit names the member whose header leaked, which is what made the inheritance diagnosable rather than merely puzzling
NOT_FIXED: adding PIPEREV to the composite KEYS tuple is a build-path change and would alter every composite's header. Owner's call, not taken here.
credit: found by the auditing session, not by the session that built the products
